newsitem.title: ISRAEL: United States condemns Hebron shooting.
newsitem.headline: United States condemns Hebron shooting.

text.p: The United States condemned a shooting spree by an off-duty Israeli soldier in Hebron that wounded seven Arabs on Wednesday. It said negotiations on the West Bank town's fate would continue.

U.S. Middle East peace envoy Dennis Ross told reporters in self-ruled Gaza: "We in the United States condemn this act on the strongest possible terms." Asked if negotiations on a long-overdue Hebron deal would continue, Ross said "Yes".

Palestinian President Yasser Arafat also condemned the shooting attack. "This is a regrettable act and we are following the details," he said after holding talks with Ross on the pending deal between Israel and the PLO under which 80 percent of Hebron is to be handed over to Palestinian self-rule. .
But Arafat did not say when or if a summit with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu would take place. "We are still negotiating," he said.
Ross said the attacker would not succeed in grounding the long-overdue Hebron deal, telling reporters: "Those who use violence cannot and must not and will not be arbiters of the future."
"We will continue to find ways to overcome the differences."
